description:
\`CachedCrl.bytes: Vec<u8>\`, \`CachedOcspResponse.bytes: Vec<u8>\`,
\`CrlCacheKey.issuer_dn_der: Vec<u8>\`, \`CrlCacheKey.distribution_point_uri: Option<String>\`,
\`OcspCacheKey.cert_serial: Vec<u8>\`, \`OcspCacheKey.issuer_key_hash: Vec<u8>\`, and
\`OcspCacheKey.responder_url: String\` are all \`pub\` fields (cache.rs:88-117,
137-170).

This pins the storage representation. Once these ship, switching to
\`Arc<[u8]>\`, \`Bytes\`, an \`smallvec\`, an interned-string type, or any
zero-copy alternative is a breaking change. Cache backends that already
hold the bytes in a more efficient representation (mmapped CRL files, an
Arc-shared blob in a Redis client, etc.) must allocate \`Vec<u8>\` for
every \`put_crl\` and the cache trait cannot return zero-copy refs without
breaking the field types.

Same constraint locks \`Vec<u8>\` as the key-byte representation in
\`HashMap\` storage, forcing custom \`RevocationCache\` impls to coerce
to/from \`Vec<u8>\` on every operation even when they natively hold
keys in a different shape.

Fix shape: make the fields private and expose getters that return
\`&[u8]\` and \`&str\`. Add private \`new(...)\` constructors. The
constructors become the only way to populate the values, which is
what cache impls already do via the parsing helpers.

Same argument applies to \`FetchResponse.bytes\`, \`FetchResponse.content_type\`,
\`FetchRequest.url\`, \`AiaUrls.ocsp\`, \`AiaUrls.ca_issuers\`,
\`OcspRequestBytes.body\`, and \`OcspRequestBytes.content_type\`.

Pre-1.0 this is the right window to make these private. Post-1.0
the cost of every \`Vec<u8>\` allocation in the per-request hot path
multiplied by the number of CRL/OCSP checks per validation per RPS
adds up.
title: Public Vec<u8> / String fields on CachedCrl / CachedOcspResponse / *CacheKey lock storage representation
